items.title: FLEX: Flame Extinguishment Experiment (PSI-69)
items.text: Objective: Burns isolated methanol and heptane droplets in microgravity across oxygen, pressure and diluent (CO2, helium) levels to find when flames go out, informing the choice of gaseous fire suppressants for spacecraft cabins. Hardware: CIR / MDCA. Sensors: backlit droplet camera, color flame camera, OH* chemiluminescence camera, radiometers. Measured: droplet initial diameter, flame extinction diameter, burning rate, burn time, test end (extinction, disruption, completion). The loaded table has 274 test rows. Oxygen ranged from 12 to 34 % across 274 tests. Pressure ranged from 0.7 to 3.09 bar across 273 tests. Fuels or materials by number of tests: methanol 157, heptane 117. Test outcomes: extinguished 186, disrupted 61, burned to completion 27. 104 tests ran close to the ISS cabin atmosphere (21 % O2, 1.013 bar). 17 tests ran close to the Lunar habitat atmosphere (30 % O2, 0.703 bar). 104 tests ran close to the Mars transit vehicle atmosphere (21 % O2, 1.013 bar). Fire-safety role: suppression. Fuel phase: liquid. DOI 10.60555/mbq8-0451.

items.title: CFI-G: Cool Flames Investigation with Gases (PSI-159)
items.text: Objective: Studies normal and inverse spherical gas flames (ethane, propane, butane) from a porous burner over a wide range of oxygen and pressure, recording ignition, self-extinction and cool-flame behaviour relevant to gas leaks in oxygen-enriched cabins. Hardware: CIR / ACME burner. Sensors: color camera, photomultiplier tube, burner thermocouple. Measured: hot ignition, burn time, self-extinction vs flow termination, peak burner temperature, cool flame presence. The loaded table has 333 test rows. Oxygen in the burner stream of inverse flames ranged from 12 to 85 % across 154 tests. Oxygen in the chamber atmosphere of normal flames ranged from 17.97 to 39.97 % across 179 tests. Pressure ranged from 0.5 to 3.31 bar across 333 tests. Fuels or materials by number of tests: butane 140, propane 99, ethane 94. Outcomes of inverse flames: self extinguished 81, sustained until stopped 58, no ignition 15. Outcomes of normal flames: self extinguished 102, no ignition 46, sustained until stopped 31. 35 normal-flame tests ran close to the ISS cabin atmosphere (21 % O2, 1.013 bar). 15 normal-flame tests ran close to the Exploration atmosphere atmosphere (34 % O2, 0.565 bar). 15 normal-flame tests ran close to the Pressurized rover atmosphere (34 % O2, 0.565 bar). 35 normal-flame tests ran close to the Mars transit vehicle atmosphere (21 % O2, 1.013 bar). Program: ACME. Fire-safety role: flame behavior. Fuel phase: gas. DOI 10.60555/cyt1-kh64.

items.title: BASS-II: Burning and Suppression of Solids II (PSI-25)
items.text: Objective: Burns solid materials (PMMA rods, films and slabs, SIBAL cotton-fiberglass, Nomex) in a small flow duct at reduced oxygen and varying airflow to study flame spread, flammability limits and extinction of spacecraft materials. Hardware: MSG. Sensors: video cameras, radiometer, O2 sensor, CO2 sensor, CO sensor. Measured: initial and final O2, initial and final CO2, initial and final CO, flow device settings, video frames. The loaded table has 129 test rows. Oxygen ranged from 13.6 to 22.2 % across 129 tests. Fuels or materials by number of tests: PMMA 98, SIBAL 27, Nomex 3, wax 1. The table records no flame-out outcome column. Fire-safety role: prevention. Fuel phase: solid. DOI 10.60555/4qc4-de67.

items.title: BASS: Burning and Suppression of Solids (PSI-26)
items.text: Objective: Examines how solid materials such as PMMA spheres and slabs, SIBAL fabric, Nomex and wax candles burn and extinguish in microgravity under different flow conditions. Hardware: MSG. Sensors: video cameras, radiometer. Measured: sample material, sample geometry. The loaded table has 122 test rows. Fuels or materials by number of tests: PMMA 78, wax 23, SIBAL 12, Nomex 6, Ultem 2. The table records no flame-out outcome column. Fire-safety role: prevention. Fuel phase: solid. DOI 10.60555/58h4-dy80.

items.title: SAME-R: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment - Reflight (PSI-101)
items.text: Objective: Heats spacecraft materials (Kapton, silicone, Teflon, Pyrell, lampwick) to produce smoke, ages it and measures the particles to guide the design of spacecraft smoke detectors. Hardware: MSG. Sensors: P-Trak particle counter, spacecraft smoke detectors. Measured: inlet velocity, heater Rt/R0, duration, aging time. The loaded table has 109 test rows. Fuels or materials by number of tests: Kapton 29, Silicone 22, Lampwick 20, Pyrell 20, Teflon 18. The table records no flame-out outcome column. Fire-safety role: detection. Fuel phase: solid. DOI 10.60555/2np7-jv14.

items.title: Saffire-I: Spacecraft Fire Experiment I (PSI-98)
items.text: Objective: Burned a large cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) sheet, about 0.4 m by 1 m, inside an uncrewed Cygnus vehicle after it left the ISS, to measure large-scale flame spread and its effect on cabin atmosphere. Hardware: Cygnus (Saffire). Sensors: video cameras, O2 sensor, CO2 sensor, radiometers, thermocouples. Measured: flame spread, cabin pressure, cabin O2 and CO2. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Program: Saffire. Fire-safety role: prevention. Fuel phase: solid.

items.title: Saffire-II: Spacecraft Fire Experiment II (PSI-99)
items.text: Objective: Ignited nine 5 cm by 30 cm samples, including cotton-fiberglass, Nomex and PMMA, inside a Cygnus vehicle to test material flammability at spacecraft scale. Hardware: Cygnus (Saffire). Sensors: video cameras, O2 sensor, CO2 sensor, radiometers, thermocouples. Measured: material flammability, flame spread, cabin O2 and CO2. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Program: Saffire. Fire-safety role: prevention. Fuel phase: solid.

items.title: Saffire-III: Spacecraft Fire Experiment III (PSI-100)
items.text: Objective: Repeated the large-scale Saffire-I cotton-fiberglass burn inside a Cygnus vehicle under a different airflow condition. Hardware: Cygnus (Saffire). Sensors: video cameras, O2 sensor, CO2 sensor, radiometers, thermocouples. Measured: flame spread, cabin pressure, cabin O2 and CO2. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Program: Saffire. Fire-safety role: prevention. Fuel phase: solid.

items.title: SAME: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (PSI-102)
items.text: Objective: First ISS flight of the smoke experiment: measured the particle size of smoke from overheated spacecraft materials to judge how well spacecraft smoke detectors work. Hardware: MSG. Sensors: particle counters, spacecraft smoke detectors. Measured: smoke particle size, particle number concentration. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Fire-safety role: detection. Fuel phase: solid.

items.title: DAFT: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test (DAFT)
items.text: Objective: Checked on the ISS that a commercial particle counter works in long-duration microgravity and measured the station's background dust, which can cause false smoke-detector alarms; a risk-reduction step for SAME. Hardware: ISS cabin (portable). Sensors: P-Trak particle counter, Dust-Trak, ionization smoke detector. Measured: particle number concentration, dust mass concentration. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Fire-safety role: detection.

items.title: BRE: Burning Rate Emulator (ACME-BRE)
items.text: Objective: Uses gas flames from a porous burner to emulate burning solids and liquids, to understand materials flammability, extinction and the conditions needed for sustained burning. Hardware: CIR / ACME burner. Sensors: color camera, radiometer, heat flux gauges, thermocouples. Measured: heat flux, extinction conditions, burner temperature. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Program: ACME. Fire-safety role: flame behavior, prevention. Fuel phase: gas.

items.title: s-Flame: Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames (ACME-SFLAME)
items.text: Objective: Studies spherical diffusion flames to predict the structure, dynamics and extinction of soot-free and sooty flames. Hardware: CIR / ACME burner. Sensors: color camera, radiometer, thermocouples. Measured: flame size, extinction, radiative emission. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Program: ACME. Fire-safety role: flame behavior. Fuel phase: gas.

items.title: Flame Design: Flame Design (ACME-FLAMEDESIGN)
items.text: Objective: Investigates soot inception and control to design robust, soot-free non-premixed flames, including oxygen-enriched combustion. Hardware: CIR / ACME burner. Sensors: color camera, radiometer. Measured: soot formation, flame size. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Program: ACME. Fire-safety role: flame behavior. Fuel phase: gas.

items.title: CLD Flame: Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame (ACME-CLD)
items.text: Objective: Extends the range of flame conditions that models predict accurately by checking chemical kinetic and soot formation submodels on coflow flames. Hardware: CIR / ACME burner. Sensors: color camera, soot imaging. Measured: flame shape, soot volume fraction. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Program: ACME. Fire-safety role: flame behavior. Fuel phase: gas.

items.title: E-FIELD Flames: Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames (ACME-EFIELD)
items.text: Objective: Examines how flames produce ions and how applied electric fields can control non-premixed flames. Hardware: CIR / ACME burner. Sensors: color camera, ion current probe. Measured: ion current, flame shape. No test table is loaded for this investigation; the evidence is its published description. Program: ACME. Fire-safety role: flame behavior. Fuel phase: gas.

items.title: Summary of FLEX
items.text: FLEX burned isolated methanol (157 tests) and heptane (117 tests) droplets in microgravity while varying oxygen (12-34 %), pressure (0.7-3.09 bar) and diluent gases, measuring droplet size, flame extinction diameter, burning rate and burn time. Across 274 tests, flames extinguished in 186 cases, were disrupted in 61 and burned to completion in 27, including 104 tests at ISS-like conditions (21 % O2, 1.013 bar) and 17 tests at Lunar-habitat conditions (30 % O2, 0.703 bar).

items.title: Summary of CFI-G
items.text: CFI-G studied normal and inverse spherical gas flames (ethane, propane, butane) from a porous burner in microgravity across 333 tests at 0.5-3.31 bar. Normal flames (17.97-39.97 % chamber oxygen): 102 self-extinguished, 46 did not ignite, 31 burned until stopped. Inverse flames (12-85 % burner-stream oxygen): 81 self-extinguished, 58 burned until flow stopped, 15 did not ignite.

items.title: Summary of BASS-II
items.text: BASS-II burned solid spacecraft materials (PMMA rods, films and slabs, SIBAL cotton-fiberglass, Nomex) in a reduced-oxygen flow duct and recorded oxygen, CO₂ and CO levels, flow settings and video frames for 129 microgravity tests. The data span oxygen concentrations from 13.6 % to 22.2 % and include 98 PMMA, 27 SIBAL, 3 Nomex and 1 wax test, but the table does not contain a flame-out outcome column.

items.title: Summary of BASS
items.text: BASS (Burning and Suppression of Solids) investigated how solid materials—including PMMA spheres and slabs, wax candles, SIBAL fabric, Nomex and Ultem—burn and extinguish in microgravity under varied flow conditions using MSG hardware, video cameras and a radiometer. The published test table contains 122 microgravity runs, with 78 PMMA, 23 wax, 12 SIBAL, 6 Nomex and 2 Ultem tests, but it does not record a flame-out outcome column, so the evidence is the description of the test matrix.

items.title: Summary of SAME-R
items.text: SAME-R investigated heating spacecraft materials (Kapton, silicone, Teflon, Pyrell, lampwick) to generate and age smoke, measuring particle counts with a P-Trak counter and spacecraft smoke detectors. The 109-row test matrix records inlet velocity, heater resistance, duration and aging time for those five materials (Kapton 29, silicone 22, lampwick 20, Pyrell 20, Teflon 18) to inform detector design; no flame-out outcome column is included.

items.title: Summary of Saffire-I
items.text: Saffire-I burned a large cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) sheet about 0.4 m × 1 m inside an uncrewed Cygnus vehicle after departure from the ISS to study large-scale flame spread in microgravity. The experiment recorded flame spread, cabin pressure, and O₂ and CO₂ levels using video, gas sensors, radiometers and thermocouples, providing data on fire behavior and atmospheric changes for spacecraft safety.

items.title: Summary of Saffire-II
items.text: Saffire-II ignited nine 5 cm × 30 cm samples of cotton-fiberglass, Nomex and PMMA inside a Cygnus vehicle to assess material flammability at spacecraft scale. The experiment recorded flame spread, material flammability, and cabin O₂ and CO₂ using video, gas sensors, radiometers and thermocouples, with the evidence provided by its published description rather than a test table.

items.title: Summary of Saffire-III
items.text: Saffire-III repeated the large-scale cotton-fiberglass burn from Saffire-I inside a Cygnus vehicle but under a different airflow condition, using video, O₂, CO₂, radiometer and thermocouple sensors to monitor flame spread, cabin pressure and gas concentrations. The investigation provides only a published description of these measurements, with no test table loaded.

items.title: Summary of SAME
items.text: SAME (Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment) tested smoke from overheated spacecraft materials on the ISS, measuring particle size and number concentration with MSG hardware, particle counters and spacecraft smoke detectors. The published description provides evidence that these measurements were intended to evaluate how well spacecraft smoke detectors work in microgravity.

items.title: Summary of DAFT
items.text: DAFT tested a commercial particle counter and related sensors on the ISS to verify operation in long-duration microgravity and to measure background dust that can trigger false smoke-detector alarms, a risk-reduction step for spacecraft fire safety. The investigation recorded particle number and dust mass concentrations, but no test table is available; the evidence is the published description.

items.title: Summary of BRE
items.text: The ACME-BRE investigation uses a CIR/ACME porous burner to generate gas flames that emulate burning solids and liquids, allowing study of material flammability, extinction and sustained-burn conditions. Sensors such as a color camera, radiometer, heat-flux gauges and thermocouples record heat flux, extinction conditions and burner temperature to inform spacecraft fire-safety design. The evidence is the published description, as no test table is loaded.

items.title: Summary of s-Flame
items.text: The s-Flame (Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames) investigation studied spherical diffusion flames using a CIR/ACME burner to predict flame structure, dynamics and extinction for both soot-free and sooty conditions. Measurements of flame size, extinction behavior and radiative emission were made with a color camera, radiometer and thermocouples, and the evidence is the published description rather than a test table.

items.title: Summary of Flame Design
items.text: The Flame Design investigation tested soot inception and control in non-premixed, oxygen-enriched flames using a CIR/ACME burner and recorded flame size and soot formation with a color camera and radiometer. The published description provides evidence that the study measured soot formation and flame size to inform robust, soot-free flame designs for spacecraft fire safety.

items.title: Summary of CLD Flame
items.text: The ACME-CLD investigation tested a coflow laminar diffusion flame using a CIR/ACME burner and recorded flame shape and soot volume fraction with a color camera and soot imaging. The results extend the range of flame conditions that chemical kinetic and soot formation submodels can predict accurately, supporting spacecraft fire-safety modeling. The evidence is the published description, as no test table is loaded.

items.title: Summary of E-FIELD Flames
items.text: The ACME-EFIELD investigation examined how laminar diffusion flames generate ions and how applied electric fields can be used to control non-premixed flame shape, using a CIR/ACME burner with a color camera and ion-current probe to measure ion current and flame geometry. Because no test table is available, the evidence for these findings is the published description of the experiment.

items.title: Suppression implication SUP-1
items.text: Seventeen FLEX droplet tests at 30-34 % O₂ and 0.71-0.72 bar, matching the planned lunar habitat atmosphere of 30 % O₂ at 0.703 bar, resulted in 0 extinguished, 15 disrupted, and 2 burned to completion, with the flame never going out before the droplet was consumed or broke apart. In an atmosphere close to the planned lunar habitat, droplet flames did not go out by themselves, so a fire there should not be expected to self-extinguish and needs active suppression.

items.title: Suppression implication SUP-2
items.text: At 15 % O2 or less, 45 of 48 FLEX droplet flames were extinguished, while above 25 % O2 only 2 of 24 FLEX droplet flames were extinguished, showing that lowering oxygen is the strongest single driver of droplet flame extinction in FLEX. Lowering oxygen strongly favours extinction of droplet flames.

items.title: Suppression implication SUP-3
items.text: FLEX tested CO2 dilution in 123 tests and helium dilution in 50 tests; at 15–21 % O2 flames were extinguished in 63 of 75 CO2-diluted, 32 of 39 helium-diluted, and 26 of 44 tests without diluent, and model shows CO2 and helium affect extinction. At the same oxygen level, CO2 or helium dilution went with more extinctions, which supports diluent gases as suppressants; other test conditions were not held fixed.

items.title: Prevention implication PRE-1
items.text: In 20 CFI-G normal-flame tests at 30 % O₂ or higher and 0.703 bar or less, the flame was burning when the test ended in 5 cases, self-extinguished in 13 cases, and did not ignite in 2 cases, while flames burned gaseous fuel in atmospheres up to 39.97 % O₂. Some gas-leak flames in a lunar-habitat-like atmosphere kept burning until the test ended, so leaks still need to be stopped quickly.

items.title: Prevention implication PRE-2
items.text: Highest oxygen level in BASS-II solid-material tests is 22.2 % O2, BASS table lacks oxygen column, lunar habitat plan is 30 % O2, exploration atmosphere is 34 % O2, and loaded PSI tables have no solid-material flammability tests at habitat oxygen levels, a data gap. Solid-material flammability at habitat oxygen levels is a data gap in the loaded tables.

items.title: Prevention implication PRE-3
items.text: Saffire I, II and III burned material samples inside uncrewed Cygnus vehicles after they left the ISS; Saffire I burned a cotton-fiberglass (SIBAL) sheet about 0.4 m by 1 m to measure flame spread and cabin atmosphere effects, and the results are in published Saffire documents. Large-scale burn results are in the Saffire documents and should be read alongside the loaded tables.

items.title: Detection implication DET-1
items.text: SAME-R ran 109 smoke tests on spacecraft materials—Kapton 29, Silicone 22, Lampwick 20, Pyrell 20, Teflon 18—and the detector results are reported in the cited SAME-R documents, not in the table. The table shows which spacecraft materials were used to make smoke; detector performance must be read from the SAME-R documents.

items.title: Detection implication DET-2
items.text: The first ISS smoke experiment measured particle size of smoke from overheated spacecraft materials to assess detector performance, and the DAFT check verified a particle counter in long-duration microgravity and measured station background dust that can cause false alarms, with results described only in documents. Smoke detectors in spacecraft must handle real smoke particle sizes and background dust that can cause false alarms; the measured results are in the documents.
